findings.summary: The abstract factory pattern provides a way to create families of related objects without specifying their concrete classes. It encapsulates a group of individual factory objects that share a common theme, allowing client code to request objects through generic interfaces. This pattern separates object creation details from general usage, enabling interchangeable implementations at runtime. While it promotes flexibility and reusability, it may introduce unnecessary complexity in initial code writing and can make systems harder to debug and maintain due to higher levels of abstraction.

mechanisms.title: Encapsulated Factory Group
mechanisms.explanation: The pattern encapsulates multiple factory objects under a common abstract factory interface, each capable of creating a family of related products. The client interacts only with the abstract factory, remaining unaware of concrete implementations.

mechanisms.title: Runtime Object Creation via Interface
mechanisms.explanation: Object creation is delegated to factory methods exposed through a generic interface. The client requests objects from the factory without knowing concrete types, enabling runtime substitution of implementations.
